QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_7

question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer invested INR 5 crore in Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund on 01-Jan with a 1-year soft lock (2% exit load within 12 months, nil thereafter). He redeems on 01-Aug same year at NAV giving gross exit value INR 6 crore. What is the net proceed after soft-lock exit load, ignoring taxes?

answer.text: INR 6.00 crore — soft lock applies only to capital, not gains
INR 5.88 crore — 2% load on gross exit value of INR 6 cr
INR 5.90 crore — 2% load applied on INR 5 cr invested principal
INR 4.90 crore — 2% on invested capital plus profit clawback

explanation.text: The Logic: A soft lock-up typically applies the exit load to the GROSS REDEMPTION VALUE (NAV × units) during the lock window. 2% × INR 6 crore = INR 12 lakh; net proceed = INR 6 crore − INR 12 lakh = INR 5.88 crore. This is the PPM-standard formulation; some funds load on NAV-at-subscription, but the gross-value convention is the common Cat III hedge-fund practice. The Trap: Option A misreads soft lock as waivable on gains. Option C loads on invested principal (less common, always check PPM wording). Option D invents a profit clawback — no such mechanism in soft locks. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests lock-up types. XIX-E tests load math. Contrast with Cat I/II closed-ended AIFs (XIX-D) — no redemption/lock because they are closed-ended with no redemption window. Manager's Pro-Tip: Exit loads in Cat III PPMs should credit BACK to the remaining investors (not to the manager as additional revenue) — this is the fair-NAV principle. Clearly codify in the PPM whether load is on gross NAV or on invested capital; mismatch creates investor disputes at redemption.
